The university complex in the historical center of Freiburg contains such picturesque buildings as the [Jugendstil](/wiki/Jugendstil "Jugendstil") *Kollegiengebäude I*(short: "KG I"), built in 1911 by Hermann Billing, and the [gothic revival](/wiki/Gothic_Revival_architecture "Gothic Revival architecture") old university library. The current [University Library](/wiki/University_Library_Freiburg "University Library Freiburg") is also located in the historical center; it is a monumental building erected in the 1970s, and was to be renovated and redesigned beginning in September 2008.[[6]](#cite_note-6) It is one of the largest in Germany and placed fourth in an October 2007, German national ranking of university libraries.[[7]](#cite_note-7)

The [University Church](/wiki/University_Church,_Freiburg "University Church, Freiburg"), located across from *Kollegiengebäude II* (short: "KG II"), was built in 1683 by the [Jesuit order](/wiki/Jesuits "Jesuits"). The church and the Jesuit college were handed over to the university after the [Jesuit order was suppressed](/wiki/Suppression_of_the_Society_of_Jesus "Suppression of the Society of Jesus") in 1773. The church was destroyed in the 27 November 1944, bombing raid on Freiburg, and reconstructed in 1956.

A [restricted free agent](/wiki/Restricted_free_agent "Restricted free agent") in the 2008 offseason, Fitzpatrick signed his one-year tender offer from the Bengals on April 17.

Due to an elbow injury to starting quarterback [Carson Palmer](/wiki/Carson_Palmer "Carson Palmer"), Fitzpatrick made his first Bengals start on September 28, 2008, against the [Cleveland Browns](/wiki/2008_Cleveland_Browns_season "2008 Cleveland Browns season"). Fitzpatrick was not only the leading passer but also the leading rusher in the 20–12 loss, finishing with 156 passing yards, a touchdown, and three interceptions to go along with 41 rushing yards.[[27]](#cite_note-27) Palmer returned the next week to start against the [Dallas Cowboys](/wiki/2008_Dallas_Cowboys_season "2008 Dallas Cowboys season"), but once again had to sit the following week to rest his elbow.[[28]](#cite_note-28) On October 12, 2008, Fitzpatrick got the start against the [New York Jets](/wiki/2008_New_York_Jets_season "2008 New York Jets season") and every other game for the rest of the season.

Fitzpatrick finished the season with 1,905 passing yards, eight touchdowns, and nine interceptions to go along with 60 carries for 304 yards and two touchdowns in 13 games and 12 starts.[[29]](#cite_note-29) His 304 rushing yards ranked third among quarterbacks behind [Tyler Thigpen](/wiki/Tyler_Thigpen "Tyler Thigpen") and [David Garrard](/wiki/David_Garrard "David Garrard").[[30]](#cite_note-30)

The England team at the [2006 FIFA World Cup](/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup "2006 FIFA World Cup")

[Peter Taylor](/wiki/Peter_Taylor_(footballer,_born_1953) "Peter Taylor (footballer, born 1953)") was appointed as caretaker manager for one match, before [Sven-Göran Eriksson](/wiki/Sven-G%C3%B6ran_Eriksson "Sven-Göran Eriksson") took charge between 2001 and 2006, and was the team's first non-English manager.[[46]](#cite_note-46)[[47]](#cite_note-47) Although England's players in this era were dubbed a "[golden generation](/wiki/Golden_Generation_(English_football) "Golden Generation (English football)")" and only lost five competitive matches during Eriksson's tenure,[[48]](#cite_note-48) they exited at the quarter-finals of the [2002 World Cup](/wiki/2002_FIFA_World_Cup "2002 FIFA World Cup"), [Euro 2004](/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2004 "UEFA Euro 2004") and the [2006 World Cup](/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup "2006 FIFA World Cup").[[49]](#cite_note-49) In January 2006 it was announced that Eriksson would leave the role following that year's World Cup.[[50]](#cite_note-50) [Steve McClaren](/wiki/Steve_McClaren "Steve McClaren") was selected to succeed Eriksson, but was sacked on 22 November 2007 after just 18 matches in charge as England failed to qualify for [Euro 2008](/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2008 "UEFA Euro 2008").[[51]](#cite_note-51) McClaren was criticised for his team selection in his final game – a decisive qualifier against [Croatia](/wiki/Croatia_national_football_team "Croatia national football team") which England lost 3–2 – particularly the decision to select inexperienced goalkeeper [Scott Carson](/wiki/Scott_Carson "Scott Carson"), whose mistake lead to Croatia's first goal.[[52]](#cite_note-52)[[53]](#cite_note-53)
